claim_tested: A PH domain of the ACAP/ASAP Arf-GAP family binds PI(4,5)P2 and the binding has a catalytic consequence
key_finding: PtdIns(4,5)P2 specifically activated ASAP1/centaurin beta4 Arf GAP; D3-phosphorylated phosphoinositides were less effective; activation required PtdIns(4,5)P2 binding to the PH domain and produced a conformational change in the GAP domain detected by limited proteolysis; PH-dependent activation and membrane recruitment were separable
context: recombinant human ASAP1 fragments, in vitro GAP assay on large unilamellar vesicles; NIH 3T3 PDGF ruffle localisation
confidence_limitations: High confidence for ASAP1. ASAP1 is a paralog, not ACAP3; transfer to ACAP3 is inference from 23.0% identity and TM 0.785 structural equivalence

claim_tested: ACAP1 and ACAP2, the two closest paralogs of ACAP3, have phosphoinositide-dependent Arf GAP activity
key_finding: ACAP1 and ACAP2 were identified as Arf6 GAPs containing phosphoinositide-dependent GAP activity
context: recombinant human proteins, in vitro GAP assays; HeLa cell localisation
confidence_limitations: High confidence for ACAP1/ACAP2. The paper does not localise the lipid dependence to a specific PH-domain residue, and ACAP3 was not tested

claim_tested: Whether the BAR domain of the ACAP family carries the membrane-binding surface
key_finding: The ACAP1 BAR domain can neither bind membrane nor impart curvature; specific residues within the neighbouring PH domain are responsible for both membrane binding and curvature generation; BAR mediates BAR-BAR contacts for clustering
context: human ACAP1 BAR-PH, PDB 4NSW crystal structure plus helical cryo-EM reconstructions of protein-coated tubules; liposome assays
confidence_limitations: High confidence for ACAP1. Refutes the BAR clause of the seed hypothesis and strengthens the PH clause. Not tested on ACAP3

claim_tested: Structural definition of the inositol-phosphate pocket used as the alignment reference
key_finding: ASAP1 PH domain crystallised with diC4-PtdIns(4,5)P2 (PDB 5C79) defines a canonical C site and an atypical A site; binding to anionic lipid is cooperative and sigmoidal, unlike the hyperbolic PI(4,5)P2 binding of PLCdelta1 PH
context: recombinant human ASAP1 PH domain; X-ray crystallography, lipid binding and NMR
confidence_limitations: High confidence as the reference structure. The cooperativity means affinity cannot be read off residue counts alone

claim_tested: ACAP3 has Arf GAP activity in cells and a physiological role
key_finding: ACAP3 is a GAP specific to Arf6; knockdown abrogated neurite outgrowth in mouse hippocampal neurons and was rescued by wild type but not by a GAP-dead mutant; ACAP3 knockdown raised GTP-Arf6
context: mouse primary hippocampal neurons; HEK293T GAP assay
confidence_limitations: Establishes ACAP3 catalytic activity in cells but does not test lipid binding, PH-domain mutants, or lipid dependence of the GAP activity

claim_tested: Does the ACAP3 PH domain present a basic surface at the position of the bound inositol phosphate
key_finding: TM-align style superposition of AF-Q96P50-F1-v6 residues 258-375 onto three ligand-bound PH domains gives TM 0.785 (ASAP1 5C79), 0.698 (GRP1 1FGY) and 0.600 (PLCdelta1 1MAI). The same ACAP3 surface is recovered each time: K277, R278, A279, S280, N281, Y300, K302, T309. Basic residues in the 5 A ligand shell: ACAP3 4/12 vs ASAP1 6/13; ACAP3 3/8 vs PLCdelta1 6/11; ACAP3 4/12 vs GRP1 7/18
context: AlphaFold model of human ACAP3 PH domain vs PDB 5C79, 1MAI, 1FGY
confidence_limitations: Computational only. Sequence identity is 17-25%, so side-chain positions are approximate; AlphaFold side chains are not experimentally determined; no energy calculation or docking was performed

claim_tested: Are the mapped basic pocket residues conserved across vertebrate ACAP3 orthologs
key_finding: Across 91 vertebrate ACAP3 orthologs retrieved from UniProt (taxon 7742, non-fragment): K277 100%, R278 100%, N281 100%, K339 100%, Y300 100% (88 scored), K302 100% (88 scored), R289 98.9%, K303 95.6%. F283 is Phe in 100% of orthologs, so the loss of the ASAP1 R354 arginine is a fixed feature of the ACAP branch rather than a human peculiarity. A307 is only 27.5% Ala
context: UniProt ACAP3 orthologs, Smith-Waterman mapping of human positions
confidence_limitations: Conservation shows purifying selection at these positions but does not prove the function under selection is lipid binding

claim_tested: Does the BAR domain carry a basic concave surface
key_finding: Screened-Coulomb potential (eps 78, Debye length 8 A, probes 6 A above the surface, probes within 4 A of protein discarded) on BAR dimers: concave minus convex = +0.313 kcal/mol/e for amphiphysin (1URU, positive control, with K132, K133, K134, K137, R140 all correctly assigned to the concave face), -0.021 for the ACAP1 BAR dimer (4NSW) and +0.220 for ACAP3 BAR modelled on the 4NSW dimer (TM 0.854, 228 aligned residues, 45.2% identity)
confidence_limitations: The ACAP3 value depends on an assumed ACAP1-like dimer built from an AlphaFold monomer and is a lead, not a measurement. A simpler residue-count metric failed the amphiphysin positive control and was discarded

claim_tested: Is a BAR domain annotated in human ACAP3
key_finding: InterPro assigns IPR004148 (BAR) at residues 3-236, IPR042695 (ACAP3 BAR) at 16-215, CDD cd07637 at 16-215 and Pfam PF16746 at 3-236. UniProt Q96P50 does not carry a BAR domain feature, while UniProt records for ACAP1 and ACAP2 do
confidence_limitations: Database-level evidence. The gap is an annotation inconsistency in UniProt, not a biological difference; worth a curation lead
